Consult Summary:
- Telehealth visit for worsening, widespread pruritic, dry, erythematous rash consistent with eczema flare over several days.
- No fever or joint pain. Plan: start antihistamine (fexofenadine) and stronger topical steroid (Betnovate); continue emollients; follow-up in 2 weeks or sooner if worsening.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Widespread eczema flare
  - Timeline: Past few days; “way worse” than usual.
  - Distribution: Chest, hands, arms; worst at inner elbows (antecubital fossae).
  - Symptoms: Very itchy, dry, sore; skin cracks present. No weeping reported. No thickened/lichenified skin. No scratch marks reported.
  - Pertinent negatives: No fever; no joint pains.
  - Current management: Emollients (Diprobase cream; “Dermal” shower product). Previously tried OTC hydrocortisone; not helping. Previously tried OTC antihistamine (likely cetirizine) without benefit; not currently taking antihistamines.
  - Assessment: Extensive atopic dermatitis flare without signs of secondary infection described.
  - Plan per consult: Start fexofenadine; start Betnovate topical twice daily for ~2 weeks using small amounts (fingertip unit guidance). Continue emollients (Dermal soap and emollient). Return if no improvement or adverse reaction.

Issue 2:
- Asthma (intermittent), currently asymptomatic
  - Medications: Uses blue inhaler as needed; not daily. Breathing currently OK.
  - No acute respiratory concerns during this visit.

Issue 3:
- Family history
  - Mother with migraine.
  - Thyroid disease in mother described as “hypothyroidism” by patient; clinician later documented “hyperthyroidism” (conflict noted).

Medications:
- Diprobase (emollient) — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- “Dermal” shower product — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Hydrocortisone (OTC topical) — dose/route/frequency not documented; reported not helping.
- Blue inhaler for asthma (likely short-acting bronchodilator) — dose/route/frequency not documented; used as needed.
- New: Fexofenadine — dose/route/frequency not documented.
- New: Betnovate (topical steroid) — apply small amounts twice daily for ~2 weeks as advised.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Past Medical History:
- Eczema.
- Asthma.

Social History:
- Not discussed.

Preventative History:
- Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- Exam findings: Not performed/recorded (telehealth). Patient reports no weeping, no fever, no joint pain; cracks present; no thickened skin.

Plan:
- Start fexofenadine (antihistamine). Prescription sent to pharmacy (Boots).
- Start Betnovate topical twice daily for approximately 2 weeks using small amounts (fingertip unit guidance).
- Continue emollients: continue “Dermal” wash and emollient use. Patient uses Diprobase; clinician referenced “diprovate” (see conflict).
- Monitor for improvement; if no improvement or if adverse reactions occur, contact clinic.
- Follow-up: If worsening before 2 weeks, call sooner; otherwise reassess after 2 weeks.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):
- Missing expected elements: Full medication list reconciliation with doses/routes/frequencies; vitals; comprehensive ROS; smoking/alcohol history; vaccination and preventive care status; exact names/doses of prior steroids and antihistamines.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Family history: Patient stated mother has hypothyroidism; clinician restated as hyperthyroidism — conflict noted.
  - Emollient name: Patient uses Diprobase; clinician advised to continue “diprovate” — likely misstatement; conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Some unclear/inaudible segments and interruptions; certain medication names and details uncertain.
